key_insight: In 2D hybrid perovskite ferroelectrics, composition anisotropy creates an unexpected bulk photovoltaic field that is strongest along the non-polar vertical direction, far exceeding the polar in-plane response.
engineering_relevance: This enables new designs for voltage-readout photodetectors and ferroelectric photovoltaic devices with exceptionally large, direction-selective photovoltages.
method: Analyzed bulk photovoltaic effect behavior in 2D hybrid perovskite ferroelectrics.
Linked the response to shift-current physics and the contrast between inorganic photoactive and organic insulating layers.
Derived formulas for laser-intensity-dependent photovoltage and thickness-dependent scaling.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the vertical nonpolar EBPE is up to two orders of magnitude higher than the polar in-plane direction and among the highest reported for 2D HPFs.
watch_item: The strong anisotropic response may depend sensitively on material composition, layer orientation, and device geometry, so practical implementation will require careful alignment and reproducible fabrication.
paper_title: Composition Anisotropy Drives Large Bulk Photovoltaic Fields Along the Non-polar Vertical Direction in 2D Hybrid Perovskite Ferroelectrics
